regime.read: VIX 16.7, level GREEN: a calm tape, and stress is leaving (volatility gap easing, -0.93 over 20d). But the leadership underneath is defensive. Healthcare, Staples and Utilities hold DEPLOY grades and Technology sits at TURNING, below its 20-day average with RRG WEAKENING/DEEPENING. Every DEPLOY sector is labelled 'Momentum Fading - Hold, Don't Add'. Mixed risk-on: liquidity is supportive (falling rates, soft dollar) while risk appetite is narrow and defensive.
regime.momentum_caveat: The regime block carries only vix and level. hurst and trend are NOT in the packet, so I cannot say whether the tape is trending or MEAN_REVERT, and I make no claim either way. Two things stand in for it: option dealers are short gamma (SPY 0.35% under its flip at 775.80, QQQ 0.96% under its flip at 732.13, a knife-edge on both), and the SPY call wall at 780 is 0.89% overhead. That is a tape where moves get amplified both ways and breakouts can fail into dealer selling. Treat every momentum nomination as fragile until SPY holds above 775.80.

cross_asset.read: A short-term softening inside a firm month. It is a tailwind for breadth and commodities, but the 20-day trend has not turned yet.
Rates are falling this week, which eases liquidity. Bonds speak first, and they are speaking easier, but only on a 5-day view; the month is flat.

This is the non-confirmation. Credit lagged Treasuries by 1.49 over the month and still sits under its 20-day average. macro_weather labels it 'RISING / tightening' on the 5-day bounce; the 20-day says credit has not confirmed the equity recovery. I give the 20-day more weight.
Bid. Together with the falling yields, it fits a defensive or deflation-tilt bid more than a growth bid.
Weak. Copper is not confirming a growth upturn.
The 5-day tilt is risk-off (slowing growth); the month is still positive. Growth expectations are rolling over at the margin.
Oil up while copper is down is the inflation-shock runner-up's evidence. That combination is a squeeze on margins, not a growth signal.
Small caps lagged for the month and turned only this week. The turn is young.
LEANING RISK-ON ON LIQUIDITY, NOT CONFIRMED BY CREDIT OR GROWTH. Bonds and the dollar say easier. Credit (20d), copper and copper/gold say the growth leg is missing, and oil adds an inflation tail.

rotation.read: Tailwind. LEADING/ENTERING, DEPLOY, RS momentum 106.57, no macro headwind (0.0). Strongest sector rotation read, though the trend state is 'Fading - Hold, Don't Add'.
Leader losing pace. LEADING/EXITING, highest RS ratio 106.66, roc20 +9.28 but roc5 +0.78 (divergence -8.5). Oil +4% supports it; the momentum is rolling.
Defensive bid. IMPROVING, DEPLOY; Staples DEEPENING, Utilities EXITING. Both carry a mild macro tailwind (+0.24). Defensive leadership is a late-cycle or caution tell, not a momentum one.
The only 'Momentum Building - Add' states. All IMPROVING at HOLD. Financials carry a macro CAUTION flag (-0.24); Materials and Real Estate are neutral. Early, not proven.
Headwind, turning. IMPROVING/ENTERING but TURNING grade, below 20d SMA, macro CAUTION (-0.40).
Headwind. WEAKENING/DEEPENING, RS momentum 94.12, below 20d SMA, macro CAUTION. The market's largest weight is losing relative pace.
Mixed. IMPROVING/EXITING, HOLD, strongest macro headwind in the table (-0.40).

Biotech (LEADING/DEEPENING, 10/10 above own 20D), Enterprise Software (LEADING/DEEPENING, 17/21; capped by the TURNING Technology parent), Insurance (LEADING/ENTERING, 9/10). Also IMPROVING: Payments (8/8 but EXITING), Defense Tech, Homebuilders, Big Banks, Gold Miners (ENTERING), MedTech.

Chip Equipment (0/11 above own 20D, LAGGING/DEEPENING), Semiconductors (WEAKENING/DEEPENING, 4/15), AI Infrastructure, Infra Power (bearish H&S forming), Infra Construction (bearish descending triangle TRIGGERED), Nuclear, Space/eVTOL, Quantum, Crypto, Agri, Critical Minerals: all LAGGING. Mag7 WEAKENING with a bearish rising wedge forming.
Money is leaving the AI/semis/infrastructure complex and moving to healthcare, insurance, software and defensives. Momentum leadership is changing hands, not broadening on a single theme.

breadth.read: Young broadening with mixed leadership. Small caps -1.93% vs large caps +0.69% over 20d, but small caps +1.88% this week. The 11 sectors split 2 LEADING / 7 IMPROVING / 1 WEAKENING / 1 LAGGING: dispersion is moving out of the weak quadrants, but the IMPROVING group is mostly HOLD/TURNING grades. Breadth inside the themes is polarised, with healthcare/insurance/payments at 90-100% above their own 20D and chip equipment, nuclear, quantum and space at 0%. That is a rotation tape, not a broad advance. Crown's equal-weight/cap-weight figures agree on 'fresh, unproven': 3 days in regime, still -4.63% over 60d.
breadth.label: proxy

lean_18m: Easing rates and a softening dollar are the liquidity backdrop that tends to precede broader participation. But credit has not confirmed, copper/gold is rolling, and oil is rising. That reads as a slowing-growth, sticky-inflation mix, where leadership rotates to defensives and quality cash flows rather than high-beta growth. Lean: constructive on liquidity, wary on growth. Wait for credit to confirm before leaning hard into cyclicals or small caps.

agrees_on: Stress is easing: low VIX, volatility gap ELEVATED_EASING, no CTA size cut (share at extreme 0.11).
Broadening is young and unproven: 3 days in regime, small caps turned only this week.
Selection tape: low implied correlation and a leading DISPERSION_REGIME scenario match my polarised theme breadth and sector rotation.
Inflation-shock is the live alternative: oil up, copper/gold down and weak credit are the same evidence I see.
Dealers are on a knife-edge: SPY and QQQ both sit just under their gamma flips.
differs_on: Sizing: Crown's CTA size dial reads 1.00 (no cut). I call light, because leadership is defensive, every DEPLOY sector is 'Fading - Hold, Don't Add', Technology is WEAKENING, and credit has not confirmed. That is a poor tape for adding momentum even when stress is low.
Credit: macro_weather labels credit 'tightening' on a +0.22% 5-day move; I weight the 20-day (-1.43%, below its 20d SMA, spread -1.49) as non-confirmation.

Broadening: Crown reads it as early and constructive. I add that the small-cap leg leans into a crowded speculator long (CFTC context), and that the large-cap tech leg is actively weakening, so this is a rotation as much as a broadening.

what_would_change_it: SPY holding above its gamma flip at 775.80 (and QQQ above 732.13): dealers start damping moves, so momentum entries become less fragile. Tone moves toward normal.
High-yield credit reclaiming its 20d SMA with its 20d return turning positive: credit confirms, so the risk-on lean is confirmed.
Small caps through the Russell trend-fund flip at 2819.41 (+1.33%): CTAs turn buyer and back the broadening.
Technology RRG momentum back above 100 while the sector recovers its 20d SMA: the largest weight rejoins, and breadth stops being a rotation.

Downside: SPY losing its 760 put wall, the equal-weight/cap-weight ratio crossing back under its 20-day average (0.275009, -1.86%), or oil extending while copper/gold falls further. The inflation-shock scenario would then take the lead. Tone goes from light to defensive.
